newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger but spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger but spreads widen.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in active trade on Thursday, even as spreads to U.S. bonds widened, amid a stronger U.S. market and comments from Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen, analysts said.

"We're still lagging the U.S. so there has been some profit taking in Canadian bonds, though this whole thing was driven today by the turnaround in the U.S. market," said Hank Cunningham, a bond trader with First Marathon Securities.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.50 to C$115.90 to yield 6.709 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 14/32 to yield 6.42 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 29 basis points from 28 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

"I don't think foreign investors are as confident in the dollar continuing its rally," said Philip Strathy, vice-president with Strathy Investments Ltd. "Short-term I think the market is in a little bit of an overbought zone."
Analysts said Canadian bonds receieved some support from the release of the Bank of Canada's semi-annual monetary policy report and comments afterwards by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen.
"That put a bid into the money market right away and it seems to have followed through to the bonds," said First Marathon's Cunningham.

The bank noted in the report that there was a danger that the inflation rate would fall between the 1.0-3.0 percent target range and there may be a need for further easing in monetary conditions over the medium term.

In new issue news, the Government of Canada said it plans to auction on November 20 C$2.7 billion of 7.0 percent bonds maturing September 1, 2001. The Bank of Canada said it will buy C$405 million of the new bonds.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.45 to C$106.50 to yield 6.123 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 11/32 to yield 6.15 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to three basis points from two basis points on Wednesday.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.89 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.16 percent.
